analysis.title: International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 24, 2026)
key_insights: Asian equities rose sharply after Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia. Short covering accelerated the move, and alpha spreads appear to be performing better internationally than in the US.
The near-term bounce could extend for a few weeks, but durability into year-end is more mixed. Investors place the current market between the Liberation Day and 4Q18 analogies.

A full repeat of the post-Liberation Day rally faces skepticism. AI policy and regulatory risks, funding constraints, supply risks and monetization questions remain, and the AI infra theme could retest late-October levels. A selective approach is suggested.
The more hawkish Fed tone and softer 4Q PMIs keep the 4Q18 analogy relevant. Easing of some inflation drivers (tariffs, the Iran conflict, AI-related pressures) is a counterpoint.

JPM Global Econ 2027 Outlook sees resilient, above-trend global growth. Core inflation may stay near a 3% annualized pace in 1H27, challenging smooth disinflation expectations and pressuring central banks including the Fed.

Oil outlook: geopolitical shocks reroute oil rather than remove it. Global surpluses of 1.6 mbd in 2027 and 1.4 mbd in 2028 point to Brent in the high $70s in 1H27, high $60s in 2H27 and mid-$60s in 2028.

Oil demand could recover by 4.5 mbd in 2027, but refinery runs are expected to rise only 3.3 mbd versus the 4.1 mbd needed. Refining constraints keep product cracks elevated and limit demand growth to 3.5 mbd.

Fixed income outlook: 10-year yields forecast at 5.05% at end-1H27 and 4.95% at year-end as the Fed goes on hold. IG spreads are seen tightening to 90bp and HY to 365bp, with the default rate rising to 2.75%.
JPM is bullish on EM fixed income in 2027, forecasting sovereign spreads of 170bp and corporate spreads of 185bp, more than 30bp tighter than current levels.

JPM Global Financials conference (73 corporates, >500 investor meetings) showed a more measured tone. Themes were pricing and margin pressure, demographic and pension reform tailwinds, and cost and AI efficiency with little appetite for large M&A. European banks were noticeably less positive than last year.

Centre for European Reform takeaways: the EU is exposed to China supply shock 2.0, is on the sidelines of the AI boom, and is vulnerable to rising global bond yields. France's fiscal position and greater hedge fund ownership of sovereign debt are flagged as vulnerabilities.

JPM is tactically bullish on global equities. Broadening and ex-US have led over the past month, and EU is supported by about 13% median YoY Q3 EPS growth, level with the US, and positioning that reached extreme lows relative to the US.

A tactical Tech bounce led by US/APAC Semis and AI thematics is supported by extreme selloff metrics and valuations implying EPS cuts. The bounce is seen as technical and less V-shaped than H1 given capex peaking signs and funding pressure.
JPM Prime book data: HFs estimated down 1.5% on the day and more than 3% over 5 days, the worst since Apr 7, 2025, with MTD at -4%. Losses are beta-driven rather than alpha-driven.
HF net selling is around -2z over 20 days globally and above 2z in North America. Net leverage is at the 26th percentile over five years, but broader capitulation is not yet confirmed.

US Semis remain the most net-sold group over two months, though positioning is back near its long-term average. US net buying favored Utilities, Telecom, Pharma and Biotech, and Real Estate, a defensive rotation.

market_movers.rationale: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia triggered a sharp Asian equity rally and short covering. The note says the move reinstates the US admin's focus on equity market levels.

sector_views.rationale: Tactical bounce in US/APAC Semis and AI is supported by extreme selloff metrics and valuations, but the move is technical and short-term.
Sentiment at the financials conference was noticeably less positive than last year despite rising rates and limited asset quality concerns.
Broadening and international leadership, ex-AI rotation and strong earnings support a tactically bullish view.
US net buying favored these groups, though Consumer Staples Distribution positioning is at historical highs.

earnings_insights: Q3 median YoY EPS growth is about 13% in both the EU and the US (JPM, reported season).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Challenges smooth disinflation expectations and pressures central banks including the Fed.
Yields move modestly higher before easing once the Fed holds.
Modest decline as the Fed goes on hold.
Persistent surpluses push prices lower through 2027.
Surplus persists even after inventory accumulation in China and OECD.
Defaults rise while spreads still tighten on demand.

trade_ideas.description: Tactical long global equities, with a Tech bounce led by US/APAC Semis and AI thematics
trade_ideas.rationale: The Tech selloff screens extreme on speed of unwind, HF selling, QQQ short interest and retail sentiment, and valuations imply EPS cuts.
trade_ideas.risk: The bounce is technical and short-term. Capex peaking, funding pressure, AI ARR questions and policy uncertainty could cap it.

risk_factors: AI policy and regulatory risks, funding constraints, supply risks and monetization questions.
Peak AI capex narrative and a possible retest of late-October lows in AI infra.
A hawkish Fed and softer 4Q PMIs support the 4Q18 analog of a renewed selloff.
Broader HF capitulation is not yet confirmed and further beta-driven losses are possible.
Rising global bond yields and fiscal vulnerability in Europe, especially France.
Cyber risk and margin pressure in financials.
vol_and_positioning: HFs estimated down 1.5% on the day, more than 3% over 5 days and -4% MTD. 5d and 63d returns are below -3z.
Global HF net selling is around -2z over 20 days and above 2z in North America, with the 8wk net leverage change around -2z.
Net leverage is at the 26th percentile over five years for All Strategies.
US TPM 4wk change was about -1z, above the -1.5z capitulation trigger. The level is at the 13th percentile since 2015.
Global positioning is around the 10th percentile and -1.5z, with Japan still being sold and China/HK near lows.
US Semis positioning is at the 63rd percentile since 2018, its lowest since May 2025. HFs have sold US Semis for 6 consecutive weeks.
QQQ short interest levels and retail sentiment are screening extreme bearish.
geopolitical: The oil outlook assumes both the Iran/Middle East and Russia/Ukraine conflicts continue, with oil rerouted rather than removed.
US midterm implications include a flatter geopolitical curve in 2027 on improved prospects for the Middle East and RU/UA.
The EU faces China supply shock 2.0 and needs a united European front on China trade.
Geopolitical resolution does not appear in the cards near term.

tension_points.bull_case: Selloff screens extreme (6 weeks of HF Semi selling, high QQQ short interest, bearish retail sentiment), valuations imply EPS cuts and there are no classic cycle-peak signals.
tension_points.bear_case: Buyside capex expectations are peaking, the rotation out of AI may extend on funding pressure, and AI ARR trends and policy are uncertain. The hawkish Fed and soft PMIs keep the 4Q18 analogy alive.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI infra retesting late-October levels, or HF positioning moving to a broader capitulation without a rebound.
